d1_databases.name: acct3/harz-million-corpus
d1_databases.note: THE RECORDED '8.9GB' FIGURE = this D1 file_size (content bytes are 7.25GB; SQLite overhead/indexes make the file 23% larger)

critical_findings.finding: D1 hard ceiling: Cloudflare documents a 10GB per-database limit. The million-corpus file is at 8.93GB = 89% of the hard ceiling.
critical_findings.consequence: Real remaining headroom is ~1.07GB of file growth. At the measured overhead (1.23x) and avg content 4.47KB/doc, that is roughly 190,000 more docs — NOT the ~500k that content-byte math suggests. The wall arrives ~5x sooner than the cap ledger implies.

critical_findings.finding: The cap check compares content_bytes (meta) against cap_bytes, but actual disk consumption runs 23% higher (file_size). The sovereign 9.5GB ruling is enforced on a number 23% smaller than reality.
critical_findings.consequence: If the ruling's intent was 9.5GB of real storage, the DB will overshoot it; if the intent was 9.5GB of content, the D1 10GB hard limit bites first. Either way the binding wall is D1's 10GB, and it is close.

critical_findings.finding: DB is on paid D1 (8.9GB exceeds the free-tier 5GB/database cap); per-row read/write billing applies to all future ingestion.
critical_findings.consequence: Ingestion cost scales with rows written; batch design must minimize re-reads (dup checks) and re-writes.

critical_findings.finding: Accepted mechanisms verified in the live worker code and preserved by this procedure: 3-level dedup (content_hash + norm_hash + prefix_hash via INSERT OR IGNORE), D1 .batch() for grouped writes, meta-table ledger (total_ingested / dup_rejected / total_bytes), honest 507-style refusal at cap.
critical_findings.consequence: These are known-good and this procedure does not replace them — it wraps them.
